    Rolling-origin renewal forecast backtesting

    Source: R/outbreak-backtest.R
    epi_renewal_backtest.Rd

    At each expanding training origin, estimates a constant reproduction number from only the preceding incidence using a gamma-Poisson renewal posterior. It then forecasts horizon periods with epi_renewal_forecast() and pairs each forecast with the later observed count. In "posterior" mode, each trajectory draws a fixed future R from the training posterior; "fixed" mode uses the posterior mean. Neither model learns time variation or adjusts for imports, reporting delays, susceptible depletion, data revisions or observation error. Posterior intervals are conditional on the prior, known generation weights, model assumptions and observed history; they are not automatically calibrated.

    Usage

    epi_renewal_backtest(
  .data,
  time,
  cases,
  weights,
  initial,
  horizon = 1L,
  stride = 1L,
  mode = c("posterior", "fixed"),
  prior_shape = 1,
  prior_rate = 1,
  nsim = 1000L,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

    Arguments

    .data

    Ungrouped data frame ordered by time with one row per period.

    time

    Regular, strictly increasing numeric or whole-day Date column.

    cases

    Non-negative integer incidence counts.

    weights

    Discrete generation-interval probabilities for lags 1 onward, summing to one.

    initial

    Number of observations in the first training window; must exceed the number of generation lags.

    horizon

    Number of future periods per assessment window.

    stride

    Number of rows between successive forecast origins.

    mode

    Either "posterior" for gamma-distributed R or "fixed" for the training posterior mean.

    prior_shape, prior_rate

    Positive gamma prior shape and rate for R.

    nsim

    Number of simulation trajectories per origin, at least two.

    conf_level

    Central prediction interval probability, strictly in (0,1).

    Value

    One row per origin and future horizon, with origin/target times, observed outcome, posterior mean R and forecast mean, median and interval bounds. Each origin uses only its training observations.

    Details

    The data must be a single complete series with regular numeric or Date time. The initial period and every assessment horizon are disjoint within an origin; assessment windows from different origins can overlap and are dependent. The backtest assumes historical observations were available without delay at their time of origin. In real surveillance, use vintage data reflecting what was known at each forecast date rather than revised final counts. Set a seed for reproducible Monte Carlo forecasts.

    Examples

    d <- data.frame(day = 1:8, cases = c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128))
set.seed(1)
backtest <- epi_renewal_backtest(d, day, cases,
  weights = 1, initial = 4,
  horizon = 2, nsim = 100
)
wis(backtest, observed, forecast_median, forecast_low, forecast_high, alpha = .05)
